claims.text: The initial WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar.
As-cast WTaTiVZr is a solid-solution BCC alloy.
As-cast WTaTiVZr contains nanoscale lattice distortions.
WTaTiVZr has greater lattice distortion and chemical disorder than pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion and chemical disorder modify dislocation nucleation, mobility, and entanglement.
Plastic deformation in WTaTiVZr can be dislocation dominated.
Higher dislocation density in WTaTiVZr leads to dislocation entanglement.
Compositionally induced local stress variations facilitate dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
Chemical disorder and lattice strain promote non-catastrophic dynamic recovery.
Dislocation interactions provide strain hardening that impedes crack propagation.
The proposed dislocation interactions localize plastic deformation.
Pure tungsten has limited dislocation mobility and less effective strain hardening under the stated high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will have greater plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten above approximately 800 K.
WTaTiVZr will have greater toughness and energy absorption before crack propagation than pure tungsten above approximately 800 K.
WTaTiVZr will develop more homogeneous dislocation distributions and stronger signs of dynamic recovery than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate above approximately 800 K but may not operate at lower temperatures because dynamic recovery is less active there.
Heavy irradiation or extreme loading may introduce mechanisms not captured by the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the proposed dislocation interactions localize plastic deformation, whereas the predicted outcome calls for more homogeneous dislocation distributions. These imply opposing spatial distributions of deformation unless the intended wording was that the interactions suppress localization.
